_: A machine is not a component. It is an arrangement of them, plus the facts that only exist once they are arranged — how many of each, in which slots, and what the combination does that no part does alone. This file carries the arrangement and nothing that belongs to a part, so a component fixed here is fixed for every machine that references it.

_match._why: DMI is world-readable and present before anything else is running, so a machine can be recognised with no privilege, no agent and no network — which is the only useful moment to recognise it in.

identity._not_matched_on: serial number. That identifies one machine; this describes a model, and a profile keyed to a serial would need writing again for every unit.

components._note: two of eight slots used, 32 GB of a 1 TB ceiling. Headroom is a fact about this arrangement, not about the part.
quantity varies per unit; the profile describes the part, the site's own inventory describes what is fitted

sensors._blind_means: the part behind the sensor is absent, not that the sensor is broken. Read the count, not the names, and a machine with a GPU fitted will not have this problem.

wake_on_lan._caution: the NIC ships `Wake-on: d` while advertising `Supports Wake-on: pumbg`. Reading the capability line reports a whole fleet as ready to wake when none of it is — read the state line.

known_faults._why_here_as_well: the cost is a property of the arrangement. The controller's behaviour is the same in any box; that it accounts for 60% of this machine's electricity bill is true because this machine has no GPU and no RAID card fitted, and would not be true of one that had.

measured_on._read_this_as: one site's numbers, not a specification. They are here because a profile with no measurements in it cannot tell an operator whether their machine is behaving like the others.
